title: Texas DA Alleges ICE Deliberately Ran Over Immigrant, Accuses Agency of Suppressing Evidence
body:
A Houston‑area district attorney has accused U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement of deliberately running a police cruiser over a migrant during a routine immigration stop, and says the federal agency has been uncooperative in providing evidence that could clarify the incident. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare told reporters that his office has amassed a trove of video recordings that appear to show ICE officer Michael Gomez intentionally accelerating his vehicle into the chest of 23‑year‑old Miguel Parra Hernandez on Saturday, a maneuver that could constitute assault with a deadly weapon and a civil rights violation.

The incident unfolded on a busy intersection near the 610 Loop, where ICE agents stopped Hernandez and two companions for a status check. According to the videos collected by the Harris County Police Department, the agents ordered the three men to remain on the curb while an ICE patrol car positioned itself behind them. Witness footage shows the cruiser’s engine revving before the vehicle lunges forward, striking Hernandez’s torso. He was thrown to the ground, bleeding heavily, and required emergency transport to a local hospital. The other two men were unharmed.

Teare’s office has been conducting its own investigation, gathering body‑camera footage, dash‑cam recordings, and by‑stander videos from smartphones. “We have more than a dozen distinct angles that clearly depict the moment the vehicle made contact,” Teare said. “What is troubling is the lack of transparency from the federal agency that was directly involved.” The DA’s office has formally requested the release of the officer’s dash‑cam and internal investigative reports, as well as any communications between ICE and local law‑enforcement officials surrounding the stop. To date, ICE has neither supplied the requested material nor offered a substantive comment on the allegations.

Legal experts say the case raises complex jurisdictional questions. While ICE officers are federal law‑enforcement agents, they often operate in partnership with local police departments, especially in large metropolitan areas like Houston. “If an ICE officer intentionally uses a vehicle as a weapon, that could trigger both federal and state criminal statutes, including assault, reckless endangerment, and violations of civil‑rights statutes,” explained Professor Elena Martinez, a criminal‑law scholar at the University of Texas School of Law. “However, the interplay between federal immunity doctrines and state prosecutorial authority will likely become a focal point in any ensuing litigation.”

The incident arrives amid heightened scrutiny of ICE’s tactics nationwide. Critics have long argued that the agency’s aggressive enforcement methods—such as vehicle checkpoints and rapid‑response raids—create dangerous environments for both undocumented migrants and the broader public. Recent congressional hearings have highlighted cases where ICE’s use of force appeared excessive, prompting calls for reforms ranging from stricter oversight to the curtailment of certain enforcement activities. Advocacy groups have already rallied around Hernandez’s family, demanding an independent federal investigation and calling for the officer involved to be placed on administrative leave pending the outcome.

If the district attorney’s office proceeds with criminal charges, the case could set a precedent for state-level accountability of federal immigration officers. It may also pressure ICE to adopt more transparent evidence‑sharing protocols with local jurisdictions. “We are prepared to pursue every legal avenue to ensure justice for Mr. Parra Hernandez,” Teare affirmed, adding that the DA’s office will continue to request the missing video and any internal disciplinary records.

As the investigation unfolds, the eyes of both the legal community and immigrant‑rights advocates will be fixed on the forthcoming exchanges between Harris County prosecutors and the Department of Homeland Security. Whether the evidence will compel ICE to cooperate—or lead to a broader policy shift—remains uncertain, but the case underscores an escalating demand for accountability in immigration enforcement across the United States.
